ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within the circle $\odot O$ where the radius is 1, the chord $AB = \sqrt{2}$. Construct an equilateral triangle $\triangle ABC$ inside $\odot O$ with $AB$ as one side. Rotate $\triangle ABC$ counterclockwise around point A. When side $AC$ first touches $\odot O$ tangentially, what is the angle of rotation?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} When $AC$ is tangent to $\odot O$, connect $CO$ and extend it to meet $AB$ at point $M$, connect $AO$,\\
since $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
thus, $CM\perp AB$,\\
since $AB = \sqrt{2}$,\\
thus, $AM = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\
since $OA = 1$,\\
thus, $OM = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\
therefore, $\angle OAM = 45^\circ$,\\
since $\angle OAC'=90^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle BAC'=135^\circ$,\\
since $\angle C'AB'=60^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle BAB'=75^\circ$,\\
therefore, when $AC$ is tangent to $\odot O$ for the first time, the angle of rotation is $\boxed{75^\circ}$;

method.method_draft: Use an analytic coordinate route. From the image, take AB as the baseline chord and place A = (0,0), B = (sqrt(2),0), choosing O on the same side of AB as shown inside the circle. From the text, OA = OB = 1, so the center satisfying equal distance from A and B is O = (sqrt(2)/2, sqrt(2)/2). The initial equilateral side AC makes angle 60° with the positive x-axis AB. After a counterclockwise rotation by theta, side AC has direction angle phi = 60° + theta. The line through A in direction phi is tangent to the unit circle centered at O exactly when the distance from O to this line equals 1. Using the distance formula to a line through the origin with unit direction (cos phi, sin phi), distance = |O_x sin phi - O_y cos phi| = |sin phi - cos phi|/sqrt(2). Set this equal to 1. The first counterclockwise solution after phi = 60° is phi = 135°, so theta = 135° - 60° = 75°.

\textbf{Solution:} When $AC$ is tangent to $\odot O$, connect $CO$ and extend it to meet $AB$ at point $M$, connect $AO$,\\
since $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
thus, $CM\perp AB$,\\
since $AB = \sqrt{2}$,\\
thus, $AM = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\
since $OA = 1$,\\
thus, $OM = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\
therefore, $\angle OAM = 45^\circ$,\\
since $\angle OAC'=90^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle BAC'=135^\circ$,\\
since $\angle C'AB'=60^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle BAB'=75^\circ$,\\
therefore, when $AC$ is tangent to $\odot O$ for the first time, the angle of rotation is $\boxed{75^\circ}$;

When rotating counterclockwise around A, side AC is tangent to the circle for the first time at the tangent position passing through A; the tangent to the circle at point A is perpendicular to radius OA, so the tangent direction forms 90° with AO.
